solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

flags: minor: very easy for a Words in Context item; distractors (sporadic, cryptic, extravagant) are not tempting
S021-01.notes: Dated, labeled, cross-referenced entries = meticulous. Others contradict the colon clause.

S021-02.notes: She skips to the second sentence and 'no one ever knew' = recovered unnoticed. A contradicts 'no one knew'; B, C unsupported (she did rehearse).

S021-03.notes: Only A shows both the 2020 drop (900 to 600) and partial recovery (to 750, below 900). B is e-books; C totals; D a single point that shows no drop or trend.

S021-04.notes: Underdrawings outlining the bare patches and 'leave open' notes show the gaps were intentional. B overreaches (texts say nothing about illness); A opposite; D contradicts the conservators' own method.

S021-05.notes: Irregular plural 'children' takes 's for possessive: children's. 'childrens'' is the classic trap.

S021-06.notes: Subject 'the stone mill' needs a finite main verb; opening participial phrase is a modifier. A, B, C leave the sentence without a main verb (fragment).

flags: minor: restatement relationship is very transparent (one-tenth fuel -> nine-tenths renewable); could sit at the easy/medium border
S021-07.notes: Second sentence restates the first in complementary terms: 'In other words.' No contrast (A, D) or example (B).

S021-08.notes: Method = cameras at 40 water holes for 12 months. B, D are findings; C is the interpretation.

S021-09.notes: Flaw is an unrepresentative sample: gym members likely exercise more than residents overall. A merely restates the 20%; B could even look like support; C irrelevant to the generalization.

S021-10.notes: Established date (500 BCE via pottery) -> conflicting radiocarbon dates (800 BCE) -> explanation (pottery style persisted longer). A overstates (no recommendation to abandon); C one fort only; D pottery does not confirm the new date.
